refuted.claimed: "Towards Better Agents for Multi-Turn User Interaction: The Next User Turn Is More Than Context", arcxiv.org/abs/2608.17499
refuted.verdict: REFUTED (host fabricated, paper real). arcxiv.org is not a preprint server; no such repository exists.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2608.17499 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17499 (FACA, submitted 18 Aug 2026). Treat the rest of whatever bibliography produced this URL as suspect: a fabricated hostname is a generation artifact.

refuted.claimed: A paper developing stochastic interventions / modified treatment policies with a TEXT-valued action space and identification theory
refuted.verdict: NOT_FOUND. Searched several phrasings across arXiv full text and the web. No such paper exists as of 2026-09-19. Do not cite a precedent and do not imply identification for text-valued MTPs has been established.
refuted.replacement: None. Nearest confirmed: arXiv:2606.27518 (function-valued numeric treatments, positivity-free stochastic policies) and arXiv:2502.17538 (Q-learning DTR over a language action space, no identification theory). This is our whitespace, but it is a negative search result and must be re-checked before it is written as a novelty claim.

refuted.verdict: REFUTED. That DOI does not resolve (digit transposition).
refuted.replacement: DOI 10.1080/03610929408831393 — Robins, "Correcting for non-compliance in randomized trials using structural nested mean models", Commun. Stat. Theory Methods 23(8):2379-2412, 1994.

refuted.claimed: ROSA2 / "Words and Weights", ICML 2026
refuted.verdict: UNVERIFIED VENUE, and the title is wrong. arXiv:2603.01375 has one version, no Comments field, no journal-ref, no ICML acceptance footnote (only the template's "Machine Learning, ICML" keywords); no icml.cc/virtual/2026 page and no PMLR entry. The only assertion of ICML 2026 is the first author's personal homepage; search snippets echo it.
refuted.replacement: Cite as arXiv:2603.01375, "Words & Weights: Streamlining Multi-Turn Interactions via Co-Adaptation" (preprint, 2 Mar 2026). Ampersand, not "and". Contrast arXiv:2509.24696 (T-POP), whose v2 Comments field literally reads "Accepted to ICML 2026" — that is what evidence looks like.

refuted.claimed: ProRefine, NeurIPS 2025
refuted.verdict: OVERSTATED VENUE. It is the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Efficient Reasoning, not the main conference.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2506.05305, "ProRefine: Inference-Time Prompt Refinement with Textual Feedback", NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Efficient Reasoning. Also: its "3-37 point" gain is against zero-shot CoT with 3+ LLM calls per iteration, i.e. unmatched compute.

refuted.claimed: Progressive-Hint Prompting, ICML
refuted.verdict: OVERSTATED VENUE, and miscategorized. It is the ICML AI4MATH 2024 workshop, not main ICML (6 arXiv versions over 18 months, never a main track). It is also not a self-correction method — no critic, no error detection, just answer-conditioned re-prompting with an agreement stopping rule.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2304.09797, ICML AI4MATH 2024 workshop. Cite it for the efficiency result (46.17% fewer sampled paths) and as a critic-free ablation target, never grouped with Self-Refine/Reflexion as "self-correction".

refuted.claimed: Self-Refine gives ~20% average absolute gain (used as support for multi-round reasoning improvement)
refuted.verdict: REFUTED as reasoning evidence. The gain is concentrated in preference-judged open-ended tasks (Dialogue Response 25.4->74.6, Sentiment Reversal 3.8->36.2). On GSM8K: GPT-3.5 64.1->64.1, ChatGPT 74.8->75.0, GPT-4 92.9->93.1. The paper itself blames the model's inability to detect whether an error exists.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2303.17651 (NeurIPS 2023) cited for the generate/critique/refine architecture only, with its own GSM8K row (+0.0/+0.2) quoted as honest evidence that a same-model critic does not repair reasoning.

refuted.claimed: Chen et al. CPO performs causal identification of prompt effects
refuted.verdict: OVERSTATED. DML is applied to prompt and query embeddings as nuisance-adjustment features. There is no identification theorem for the prompt-as-treatment estimand, no overlap/positivity argument for a continuous embedding-valued treatment, and it is an unrefereed preprint.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2602.01711 cited as a "DML-debiased offline reward model for query-specific prompt selection". Note the live critique: by arXiv:2602.15730's argument, running DML on prompt AND query embeddings jointly is exactly the treatment/covariate conflation that requires residualization.

refuted.claimed: Wang et al. (SCIE) gives rigorous causal identification of instruction effects
refuted.verdict: OVERSTATED. The ATE is estimated on LLM-self-generated observational data using hand-chosen interpretable textual features as the treatment representation, with no identification argument and no unconfoundedness discussion.
refuted.replacement: AAAI-25, Vol 39 No 14, pp. 15212-15220, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v39i14.33669 (preprint arXiv:2412.15314), cited only as peer-reviewed precedent that "instructions are treated as the treatment" — which is verbatim in its abstract.

refuted.claimed: Feldman et al. propose residualization of the treatment with respect to text
refuted.verdict: WRONG OBJECT, and wrong setting. It is COVARIATE residualization (covariates residualized w.r.t. treatment), and the setting is a controlled SAE-steered text experiment, so the bias is overcontrol / adjustment-set contamination, not classical observational confounding.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2602.15730 cited precisely: "conditioning on a text representation induces bias because text conflates treatment and covariate information; remedy is covariate residualization, in a randomized SAE-steered design."

refuted.claimed: LMTP relaxes positivity for continuous/high-dimensional treatments
refuted.verdict: HALF TRUE, and the price is omitted. Nothing is proven about identifying the static estimand when positivity fails. A DIFFERENT estimand (a policy applied to the natural value of treatment) is identified under a support-preservation condition on d that the analyst can enforce by construction. The cost: identification of the natural-value-dependent parameter requires STRONG sequential randomization (Assumption 3: U_{A,t} independent of future covariate AND treatment noise), not the standard condition; and for the threshold shift the parameter is not pathwise differentiable, so no sqrt(n) estimator exists.
refuted.replacement: DOI 10.1080/01621459.2021.1955691 / arXiv:2006.01366 (JASA 118(542):846-857), with the support condition attributed to Young, Hernan & Robins, DOI 10.1515/em-2012-0001, and the strong-exchangeability cost stated explicitly. Confirmed independently by the tutorial arXiv:2304.09460.

refuted.claimed: Kennedy's incremental propensity score interventions cover continuous / high-dimensional treatments
refuted.verdict: REFUTED. The treatment is binary at every time point. The no-positivity result is genuine but binary-only, and the estimand is defined through the true propensity score, so it moves if the observational treatment mechanism moves.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:1704.00211, JASA 114(526):645-656, cited as the cleanest precedent for a longitudinal estimand needing no positivity at all, explicitly scoped to binary treatments. Review: arXiv:2110.10532.

refuted.claimed: An Orthogonal Learner for Individualized Outcomes in MDPs handles discrete or continuous action spaces
refuted.verdict: REFUTED. The "discrete or continuous" generality is about STATE spaces. The construction is finite-action throughout (R[pi_e] is a sum over a in A, action propensities pi_b(a|s), a Dirac delta(A'=a) in the nuisances, overlap metric sum_a min(pi_b,pi_e), Taxi/Frozen Lake experiments). It is also off-policy EVALUATION of a fixed pi_e targeting a level (a Q-function), not a contrast and not policy optimization.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2509.26429 (ICLR 2026) cited as a doubly robust, Neyman-orthogonal, quasi-oracle DRQ-learner for OPE in finite-action, discrete-or-continuous-state MDPs.

refuted.claimed: CATE-accurate models are suboptimal for downstream decisions
refuted.verdict: OVERSTATED unconditionally. Theorem 4.1 is conditional on a RESTRICTED second-stage function class. With an unrestricted class, thresholding a correct CATE is still optimal. The paper is also strictly static and strictly binary-treatment.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2505.13092 (NeurIPS 2025) cited as "CATE-optimal second stages can be decision-suboptimal under restricted model classes", with the caveat that it must be re-derived for sequential rounds.

refuted.claimed: DeepBlip supports continuous treatments
refuted.verdict: OVERSTATED. The losses support it (squared / BCE / one-hot), but the stated Overlap assumption is written in discrete form, the blip requires a reference level 0, and every experiment is binary.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2511.14545 (ICML 2026 poster, confirmed via icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/64916; the arXiv v1 PDF still says PREPRINT) cited as a neural SNMM for CATE over time with binary/categorical treatments in practice, and with the App. C.2 (1+C)^{tau-k} backward error-propagation bound flagged.

refuted.claimed: TextGrad = arXiv:2406.07496 (bare arXiv cite)
refuted.verdict: STALE. The canonical citation is now the Nature version.
refuted.replacement: Nature 639(8055):609-616, 19 Mar 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-08661-4, "Optimizing generative AI by backpropagating language model feedback" (Crossref-verified; author list adds Pan Lu relative to arXiv v1). Keep arXiv:2406.07496 as the preprint.

refuted.claimed: GEPA is an arXiv preprint
refuted.verdict: STALE. The v2 PDF header reads "Accepted at ICLR 2026 (Oral)".
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2507.19457 v2 (14 Feb 2026), ICLR 2026 Oral. Also: the method name is GEPA (Genetic-Pareto), and it is a compound-system optimizer positioned AGAINST RL — do not paraphrase "outperform RL" as "does RL".

refuted.claimed: T2PAM is the method for test-time multi-turn policy adaptation
refuted.verdict: IMPRECISE. T2PAM is the problem framing; the algorithm is ROSA (Optimum-Referenced One-Step Adaptation). It is also a preprint / NeurIPS 2025 MTI-LLM workshop item, not a main-conference paper.
refuted.replacement: arXiv:2509.23166, cited as "T2PAM framing, ROSA algorithm", workshop/preprint.

refuted.claimed: ShareGPT as a public dataset of real human-LLM multi-turn conversations, on a par with WildChat / PRISM
refuted.verdict: UNCLEAR / do not use. No paper, no DOI, no authoritative release, no consent framework, contested provenance; the HF mirror is nominally Apache-2.0 but the uploader had no right to license OpenAI output or user content. Heavily self-selected toward showcase and jailbreak content. No labels.
refuted.replacement: Use arXiv:2405.01470 (WildChat-1M) and arXiv:2404.16019 (PRISM, NeurIPS 2024 D&B Oral) instead. ShareGPT for smoke tests only, never in a published claim.

refuted.claimed: WildChat is released under AI2 ImpACT
refuted.verdict: STALE (the paper says so; the live artifact does not).
refuted.replacement: allenai/WildChat-1M is ODC-BY and ungated. Separately: LMSYS-Chat-1M (arXiv:2309.11998) is GATED under a bespoke non-transferable, no-redistribution license and averages only ~2.0 turns — both facts matter before we build on it.

refuted.claimed: Progressive multi-round self-critique improves reasoning; "nobody has applied causal thinking to prompt optimization"
refuted.verdict: BOTH REFUTED. Intrinsic self-correction degrades: GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5->91.5->89.0, GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8->38.1, Llama-2-70b GSM8K 62.0->43.5->36.5 (arXiv:2310.01798); no successful case with prompted-LLM feedback outside exceptionally suited tasks (TACL 2024, arXiv:2406.01297); critique CONTENT is largely irrelevant to iterative gains (arXiv:2310.12397). And causal thinking has already been applied to prompt optimization: arXiv:2605.26655 (propensity-adjusted edit-level audit) and arXiv:2504.02646 (off-policy prompt policy from logged bandit data).
refuted.replacement: Drop both sentences. Cite 2310.01798 / 2406.01297 / 2311.08516 / 2310.12397 / 2601.00514 as the constraint set, and 2409.12917 (SCoRe, ICLR 2025 Oral) as the one route that works (train, do not prompt).

refuted.claimed: "Frauen et al. 2025" orthogonal meta-learners for individualized treatment effects over time; arXiv 2510.19643; arXiv 2405.21012 (IGC-Net); arXiv 2606.13156 (VLM self-correction mirage); arXiv 2605.14553 (pure-exploration bandits for prompts)
refuted.verdict: UNVERIFIED. These surfaced only as search hits or uncited references; no id was individually confirmed.
refuted.replacement: None yet. Do not put any of these in a bibliography until each id is fetched and confirmed.

refuted.claimed: Richardson & Robins (2013) SWIGs, cited as a journal article
refuted.verdict: MISCLASSIFIED. It is CSSS Working Paper 128, University of Washington — a real but unrefereed university technical report.
refuted.replacement: Cite as a working paper (https://csss.uw.edu/files/working-papers/2013/wp128.pdf), with Theorem 31 named as the source of the strong-exchangeability condition that LMTP Assumption 3 mirrors.

refuted.claimed: Minor title/attribution errors carried in the draft bibliography
refuted.verdict: CORRECTIONS. ProTeGi's real title puts "Gradient Descent" in scare quotes; "ProTeGi" appears only in the body. Item "A Simple Try Again..." carries quotation marks around "Try Again". Shani et al.'s awkward "from Preference Human Feedback" is the genuine title, not a typo. "Lin et al." (arXiv:2510.05921) is a nine-author Gasic-group paper with a v3 of 17 May 2026 — pin the version. eva (PMLR v267 ye25a) is lowercase and does not appear in its own title. RealUserSim (arXiv:2605.20204) has an internally inconsistent submission date on its abs page ("7 Apr 2026" against a 2605 identifier) — flag if cited.
refuted.replacement: Apply as written. None of items 1-3 in the multi-turn-RL batch asserts a peer-reviewed venue on its abstract page; cite all three as arXiv preprints.

closest_prior_art.paper: Kiyohara, Cao, Saito, Joachims — Prompt Optimization with Logged Bandit Data
closest_prior_art.has: Genuinely causal and off-policy: logged bandit feedback where only the logged action's reward is observed, a policy that selects a prompt PER USER CONTEXT (not task-level), and a kernel-based off-policy policy-gradient estimator that exploits sentence similarity to control variance over a huge prompt action space while bounding reward-model bias. Evaluated on personalized description generation with click feedback.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Single-turn with an immediate reward. No sequential regime, no backward induction, no time-varying confounding from earlier turns, no notion of a responding counterpart whose future behavior depends on the action. Venue unconfirmed. This is the single biggest threat to a naive "first causal prompt policy" claim.

closest_prior_art.paper: Nakamura & Imai — GenAI Powered Dynamic Causal Inference with Unstructured Data
closest_prior_art.has: Causal effects of SEQUENCES of treatment features in unstructured text: internal GenAI representations extracted, then a marginal structural model fitted with a neural architecture that jointly learns a per-feature deconfounder along the sequence; semiparametric inference with valid asymptotic CIs. Demonstrates that a feature's effect depends on its position. This is the closest existing thing to a DTR over text.
closest_prior_art.lacks: The sequence is over feature positions WITHIN a document, not over rounds of an interaction. No decision-making: it estimates effects, it does not optimize a policy or define a policy value. No responding counterpart, no time-varying confounding generated by an agent's own earlier actions. It was absent from the original task list — its omission was the biggest gap in the audit.

closest_prior_art.paper: Zhang, Wang, Dhillon — Policy Learning with a Natural Language Action Space: A Causal Approach
closest_prior_art.has: Multi-stage decision-making with a NATURAL LANGUAGE action space and an outcome observed only after a sequence of actions; Q-learning to estimate a Dynamic Treatment Regime through a single model, gradient ascent on language embeddings, plus decoding back to coherent text. Applied to mental-health intervention, hate-speech countering, sentiment transfer.
closest_prior_art.lacks: No identification argument at all: no stated exchangeability condition, no positivity/overlap analysis, no estimand definition, no estimator theory. Optimal-policy learning only — no stochastic or modified treatment policy, no OPE, no orthogonality. This is the paper that owns our framing and leaves the entire statistical layer open.

closest_prior_art.paper: Chen, Fang, Fu, Xu, Wei — Optimizing Prompts for LLMs: A Causal Approach (CPO)
closest_prior_art.has: Prompt = treatment, query = covariate, reward = outcome, embeddings = nuisance-adjustment representation. Double Machine Learning to build an offline debiased reward model, then resource-efficient search for query-specific prompts with no online LLM evaluation. The natural T=1 baseline for our setup.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Static one-shot; no sequential prompts, no time-varying confounding, no policy-value guarantee (just debiased reward plus greedy search). No identification theorem, no overlap/positivity argument for a continuous embedding-valued treatment. Unrefereed preprint. And its joint DML on prompt AND query embeddings is precisely the conflation arXiv:2602.15730 shows induces bias — a citable defect we can exploit.

closest_prior_art.paper: Ozolcer & Bae — Offline Policy Evaluation of Multi-Turn LLM Health Coaching with Real Users
closest_prior_art.has: The only OPE done on real multi-turn LLM deployment logs: 7 users, 350 turns, 280 rated. Per-turn contextual-bandit reduction over factorized decision heads (Tool: none/Search/Code/Email; Style: concise/detailed), per-turn utility mixing satisfaction, tool outcomes and engagement, SNIPS and AIPW estimators. Finds a uniform heavy-tool policy raises average value while harming an identifiable subgroup.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Propensities are RECONSTRUCTED post hoc with cross-fitted calibrated classifiers, not logged — the authors concede Tool-head calibration is only moderate, which biases IPS/SNIPS. N=7 is a pilot, so the subgroup claim is suggestive. Per-turn bandit reduction, not a sequential DTR estimand: no backward induction, no g-formula, no time-varying confounding adjustment. NeurIPS workshop.

closest_prior_art.paper: Ma, Frauen, Feuerriegel — DeepBlip: Estimating CATE Over Time
closest_prior_art.has: First neural SNMM: blip decomposition giving per-round incremental effects, a double-optimization trick replacing sequential g-estimation, Neyman-orthogonal second-stage loss, LSTM/transformer nuisances, and offline evaluation of optimal treatment policies without recomputation. ICML 2026 poster.
closest_prior_art.lacks: No text, no LLM, no language action space. Overlap stated in discrete form, blip requires a reference level 0, all experiments binary — so continuous/structured treatments are architecturally supported but never exercised. App. C.2 error propagation grows like (1+C)^{tau-k}, i.e. accuracy decays exponentially backwards along the horizon under weak overlap, which is exactly the regime a long conversation lives in.

closest_prior_art.paper: Javurek, Melnychuk, Schweisthal, Hess, Frauen, Feuerriegel — An Orthogonal Learner for Individualized Outcomes in MDPs
closest_prior_art.has: DRQ-learner derived from the efficient influence function: doubly robust, Neyman-orthogonal, quasi-oracle efficient, debiased loss (not a one-step correction) for an infinite-dimensional target; weak positivity (supp pi_e contained in supp pi_b) rather than two-sided overlap; explicitly aimed at low-overlap regimes; reduces to Shi et al. (2021) in the discrete-state unrestricted case. ICLR 2026.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Finite-action throughout despite the abstract's generality language (that generality is about STATE spaces). Off-policy EVALUATION of a fixed pi_e targeting a level (a Q-function), not a contrast and not policy optimization. Markov assumption conditions on S_t alone, a real strengthening relative to the longitudinal literature. No text.

closest_prior_art.paper: Diaz, Williams, Hoffman, Schenck — Nonparametric Causal Effects Based on Longitudinal Modified Treatment Policies
closest_prior_art.has: The identification backbone: extended g-formula in sequential-regression form, EIF, TMLE and a sequentially doubly robust estimator, handling continuous/multivariate exposures with time-varying confounding, censoring and survival. Positivity replaced by a support-preservation condition on the shift function d that is enforceable by construction.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Never addresses a text-valued action space — Assumption 1 for strings is undefined, and there is no generalized propensity / conditional density over text. Requires STRONG sequential randomization once the policy reads the natural value. Only covers policies depending on the natural value at time t (history-dependent policies need arXiv:2605.24167). Some shifts yield non-pathwise-differentiable parameters, so no sqrt(n) estimator. No effect heterogeneity per round (that needs arXiv:2509.22916).

closest_prior_art.paper: Zhao et al. — Towards Better Agents for Multi-Turn User Interaction (FACA)
closest_prior_art.has: Per-stage credit assignment in a multi-turn agent: user-to-user segments treated as decision stages, the next user turn read as noisy temporally-local evidence about the preceding segment, mapped to ternary reaction evidence, z-normalized into a reaction advantage added at lambda=0.5 to the verified terminal outcome. +5.91pp at Qwen3-8B, +10.22pp at 14B on a nine-domain tau-bench-family average against a matched outcome-only Interactive GRPO control.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Despite the framing, purely on-policy GRPO with standard ratio clipping: no importance weighting, no propensities, no off-policy correction, no estimand. The credit signal comes from PRIVILEGED simulator-internal behavioral metadata that real users do not emit, so it does not transfer to deployment logs. That combination is the clearest opening for a DTR/OPE contribution.

closest_prior_art.has: The only prompt-optimization paper of the canonical five with a genuine PER-INSTANCE mode: instance optimization improves a solution for a given query at test time (its own words), via LLM critiques backpropagated through a text computation graph, with a momentum analogue. Nature 2025, and its radiotherapy-plan application already touches medical decision objects.
closest_prior_art.lacks: The optimized object is a static ARTIFACT (answer, code, molecule, plan) refined by self-critique against a FIXED query — not a message emitted into an ongoing interaction with a counterpart whose future behavior depends on it. Zero occurrences of "causal" or "counterfactual" in 41 pages: no outcome model, no counterfactual comparison, no estimand. The "gradient" is the authors' own scare-quoted metaphor.

closest_prior_art.paper: Wu et al. — CollabLLM: From Passive Responders to Active Collaborators
closest_prior_art.has: Multiturn-aware Rewards: simulated forward rollouts of both assistant and user turns give a long-horizon value estimate used for credit assignment on a single response — the closest published analogue to a model-based DTR. ICML 2025 Outstanding Paper, and one of very few in this area validated against real humans (201 judges: +17.6% satisfaction, -10.4% user time).
closest_prior_art.lacks: The user model is prompt-based, not learned from logs, and the sim2real literature (arXiv:2601.17087, arXiv:2603.11245) shows prompt-based simulators are excessively cooperative and give uniformly positive feedback, biasing any simulator-derived value upward. Rollouts are a training-time credit-assignment device, not inference-time search. No causal estimand, no confounding adjustment, no OPE.

closest_prior_art.paper: Imai & Nakamura — Causal Inference with Generative AI: Application to Texts as Treatments (GPI)
closest_prior_art.has: The rigorous identification backbone for text-as-treatment: nonparametric ATE identification conditions, treatment text generated by the LLM so its TRUE internal representation is known and the feature of interest is disentangled from unknown confounders, an estimation strategy explicitly designed to avoid overlap violations, DML asymptotics, plus an IV extension for perception-based features.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Strictly POINT TREATMENT. No time-varying confounding, no sequential randomization, no g-formula, no modified treatment policy. Its overlap strategy comes from controlling the text-generating process, which is an alternative to our route — we must say why we are not simply doing that across rounds.

closest_prior_art.paper: Wei et al. — T2PAM / ROSA, and Wei et al. — Words & Weights / ROSA2
closest_prior_art.has: Explicit sequential framing over dialogue turns with per-turn user feedback as reward; ROSA does a one-step closed-form-style parameter update cheap enough to run mid-dialogue with a convergence-as-turns-accumulate argument; ROSA2 jointly optimizes prompt text and weights, proving co-adaptation shrinks the required parameter shift, with ~30% MATH gains and ~40% fewer turns against TextGrad and ROSA.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Greedy/one-step rules, not backward-induction optimal regimes. No identification, no estimand, no OPE, no confounding adjustment. Self-reported best-case numbers from one author cluster (Yao Shu on both; ROSA2 is the explicit sequel), so not an independent consensus. ROSA2's ICML 2026 claim is unsupported by any primary source, and both repos are bare-bones.

closest_prior_art.paper: Feldman, Venugopal, Spiess, Feder — Causal Effect Estimation with Latent Textual Treatments
closest_prior_art.has: The sharpest theoretical warning for our design: characterizes the bias from adjusting on a text representation that conflates treatment and covariate information, and fixes it with covariate residualization; SAE features as the latent treatment, end-to-end generation plus robust estimation, econ.EM register.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Point treatment in a controlled/randomized SAE-steered experiment, so the problem is overcontrol / adjustment-set contamination, not classical observational confounding, and nothing about sequences or policies. But the result transfers directly to our nuisance construction: any embedding of the prompt OR of the conversation history contains the treatment.

closest_prior_art.paper: Barnard, Huling, Wolfson — Causal Inference for Functional Treatments with Stochastic Policies
closest_prior_art.has: Proof of concept that positivity-free stochastic policies survive an INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL treatment space: function-valued exposures, modification along a single analyst-chosen basis function, temporal confounding in continuous time, asymptotic normality and rate double robustness, applied to NHANES accelerometer data.
closest_prior_art.lacks: The action space is real-valued functions, and the whole technique depends on that linear/basis structure. Text has no basis. So it supports the claim that the idea is not intrinsically scalar, and supports nothing about strings.

closest_prior_art.paper: Li et al. — What if LLMs Ate Their Words: Causal History Effects in Multi-Turn Interaction
closest_prior_art.has: Step-level COUNTERFACTUAL interventions on multi-turn dialogue history: Neutralization (replay user messages with assistant history replaced by neutral placeholders, ~3000 conversations) and Turn Surgery (intervene on one assistant turn at a time to find which positions flip failure to success). Establishes that specific assistant turns have real, selective downstream effects.
closest_prior_art.lacks: Analysis and diagnosis only — it audits, it does not optimize a per-turn message, define an estimand, or build an estimator. Cite it as motivation; our differentiator is that we optimize.

novelty_claim: We formulate the assistant's next message in an ongoing multi-round interaction as a sequential treatment and give the first identification-and-estimation framework for it: a dynamic treatment regime over a text-valued action space, with an explicit support-preservation condition in place of point-treatment positivity, sequential-ignorability conditions stated for history that the agent's own earlier actions generate, nuisances residualized so the adjustment representation does not contain the treatment, and a turn-level orthogonal off-policy estimator of the multi-round policy value from logged interactions.
novelty_weaknesses: The word "first" rests entirely on a negative search result, and two confirmed papers sit close enough that a reviewer can recast our contribution as the composition of existing pieces. Nakamura & Imai (arXiv:2605.07834) already estimate causal effects of SEQUENCES of text treatment features with a marginal structural model, a per-feature deconfounder and valid semiparametric CIs; Kiyohara et al. (arXiv:2504.02646) already learn a per-context prompt policy off-policy from logged bandit feedback with a variance-controlled estimator over a large text action space; Zhang, Wang & Dhillon (arXiv:2502.17538) already do Q-learning for an optimal DTR in a natural-language action space. Our claim survives only as the conjunction — sequential rounds AND a responding counterpart AND identification AND off-policy policy value — and every one of those four conjuncts individually belongs to someone else. Before submission, re-run the negative search, because "no such paper exists" was last checked on 2026-09-19 and is the load-bearing premise.

The statistical machinery we are promising does not yet exist for strings, and the evidence says the obvious implementations fail. LMTP's Assumption 1 (if (a_t,h_t) is in the support then (d(a_t,h_t),h_t) is too) has no definition when the action is a string, and nothing plays the role of a generalized propensity or conditional density over text — the hardest open problem in the project, and the one the closest precedent (arXiv:2606.27518) solves only by leaning on basis/linear structure that text lacks. Meanwhile arXiv:2606.05558 shows that even with EXACT per-token behavior log-probabilities, IS/WIS/DR over multi-turn text degenerate badly enough to lose to a learned world model, so our estimator's validity depends on a coarsening (factorized per-turn heads as in arXiv:2510.17173, or turn-level geometric-mean ratios as in arXiv:2511.20718) whose estimand is then no longer the text policy we claimed to evaluate. Add arXiv:2602.15730: any embedding of the prompt or the conversation history that we adjust on contains the treatment, so our own nuisances inherit the bias we are citing against CPO, and residualization in a sequential, non-randomized setting is not something anyone has shown to work.

already_done_drop: Drop "we are the first to frame the prompt/instruction as a treatment." Done three times over, and one of them is peer-reviewed: SCIE (AAAI-25, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v39i14.33669) puts "the instructions are treated as the treatment" verbatim in its abstract; CPO (arXiv:2602.01711) builds a causal reward model on that framing; and the KDD 2026 position paper (arXiv:2605.25998) states prompt-as-treatment with final outcome as reward and says doubly robust / orthogonal policy learning is directly relevant. Cite these as established framing and spend the novelty budget elsewhere.

Drop "per-instance / per-query prompt selection with a causal estimator" as a contribution. Kiyohara et al. (arXiv:2504.02646) already do off-policy, per-context prompt policy learning from logged bandit feedback with a kernel estimator built for a large text action space, and TextGrad (Nature 2025) already optimizes a per-instance object at test time. Both predate us.

Drop any plan to build a DML-debiased reward model over prompt and query embeddings. CPO already did it, and by arXiv:2602.15730's argument doing DML on prompt AND query embeddings jointly is precisely the treatment/covariate conflation that biases the estimate. Reimplementing it reproduces a known defect. Use it as a baseline and a critique target instead.

Drop "Q-learning for an optimal regime over a natural-language action space" as the contribution. arXiv:2502.17538 already does exactly that, including the embedding-space gradient ascent and decoding back to coherent text. What it leaves open is the identification and off-policy-evaluation layer — that is the only part of this component still ours.

Do not rebuild neural SNMM / blip machinery. DeepBlip (arXiv:2511.14545, ICML 2026) already replaces sequential g-estimation with simultaneous blip learning under a Neyman-orthogonal loss, with LSTM/transformer nuisances and offline policy evaluation. Extend it to a text action space; do not re-derive it.

Do not build a doubly robust orthogonal Q-learner for MDPs from scratch. arXiv:2509.26429 (ICLR 2026) derives the DRQ-learner from the efficient influence function with double robustness, Neyman orthogonality and quasi-oracle efficiency under weak positivity. The open gap is the action space (it is finite-action), not the estimator.

Drop the "diagnose which prompt edits or which turns actually matter" work package. Both halves exist: arXiv:2605.26655 does a propensity-adjusted edit-level audit across DSPy/TextGrad-style optimizers and finds systematic edit-family by task interactions, and arXiv:2609.05882 does step-level counterfactual interventions on dialogue history (Neutralization over ~3000 conversations, Turn Surgery per turn) and shows specific assistant turns selectively flip outcomes. Cite them as motivation; auditing is no longer a contribution.

Drop token-level importance weighting for multi-turn OPE. arXiv:2606.05558 implements it with exact per-token behavior log-probs (spans matched by longest-common-token-prefix to survive BPE merges) and reports that IS/WIS/DR still lose badly to a learned world model, because ratios over horizon times a vocabulary-scale action space degenerate; the authors also call exact log-probs privileged and unavailable in real deployment. Go coarse instead: factorized per-turn decision heads (arXiv:2510.17173) or turn-level geometric-mean ratios (arXiv:2511.20718).

Drop any component whose signal is the model critiquing itself with no external evidence. Five independent results close this: arXiv:2310.01798 (monotone degradation, GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5->91.5->89.0, GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8->38.1), arXiv:2406.01297 (TACL survey: no successful case with prompted-LLM feedback outside exceptionally suited tasks), arXiv:2311.08516 (failure is at detection, not repair), arXiv:2310.12397 (critique content largely irrelevant), arXiv:2601.00514 (reasoning-model "aha moments" are rare and seldom help). If a round has no external signal, name it or cut it.

Drop "jointly adapt the prompt text and the weights across turns." ROSA2 (arXiv:2603.01375) already occupies that position and even proves co-adaptation shrinks the required parameter shift, against TextGrad (words only) and ROSA (weights only). Differentiate on the decision-theoretic side or not at all.

Drop "multi-turn-aware reward via simulated forward rollouts." CollabLLM (arXiv:2502.00640, ICML 2025 Outstanding Paper) does it and validates with 201 human judges. If we want this, the differentiator must be that the user model is learned from logs and the rollout happens at decision time, not that rollouts are used at all.

Drop any plan that trusts a prompt-based user simulator as ground truth. arXiv:2601.17087 shows agent success swings up to 9 points on simulator identity alone with systematic miscalibration and subgroup-dependent gaps; arXiv:2603.11245 (451 humans, 31 simulators) shows simulators are excessively cooperative, never produce realistic frustration, give uniformly positive feedback, and that bigger models are not better simulators. A simulator is an unmeasured nuisance parameter that shifts the estimand. Either ground it in environment state (tau^2-Bench) or validate against humans with the published protocol.

Drop bandit-style best-arm identification over candidate prompts as a methodological contribution. ProTeGi (EMNLP 2023) already implements and compares UCB, UCB-E, Successive Rejects and Successive Halving. It is also not causal inference — it is an on-policy A/B test over freshly sampled candidates — so it cannot be claimed as either novel or causal.

Drop "extend MTPs to infinite-dimensional treatments." arXiv:2606.27518 did it for function-valued exposures with positivity-free stochastic policies, asymptotic normality and rate double robustness. The remaining problem is specifically that text has no basis structure — say that, rather than claiming the infinite-dimensional extension.

Drop plans to build a new multi-turn benchmark. tau-bench (2406.12045), tau^2-Bench (2506.07982), MT-Bench-101 (2402.14762) and MultiChallenge (2501.17399) cover the space, and PRISM (2404.16019) is the only public log with the X/A/R-per-person structure a DTR needs. Build on PRISM plus a human reference protocol; do not spend the project on a benchmark.
